entries.title: Overwatch
entries.definitive_edition: Original Windows service state, preserved historically

emulation.notes: Server/service replacement prevents normal official play.

primary.why: The original Overwatch released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and later Nintendo Switch, but it was replaced by Overwatch 2/current Overwatch service. Windows is the archival reference route because it had the strongest capture path, but the original service is no longer normally playable.
primary.how_to_play: No normal official play route exists for the original service after replacement. Preserve captures, patch notes, and client/service history.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PC service route, now discontinued/replaced.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate original 6v6 Overwatch with the current Overwatch 2/current Overwatch service.

entries.title: Overwatch 2

primary.why: Overwatch 2 launched as the replacement for Overwatch and later branding/current materials returned to the Overwatch name. The current service is available across Windows, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, and Nintendo Switch 2. Windows is the best archive route because it has the broadest capture/settings ecosystem.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows client through Battle.net or Steam. Document season, patch, active modes, and branding state at capture time.

all_releases.fidelity: Current PC live-service route with best capture/settings path.

all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over Windows.
